Below is a concise, evidence-backed overview of “cell line organoids” (organoids derived from established 2D cell lines), how they are built, what they can do, and how they compare with organoids derived from fresh tissues or iPSCs.

Overview and definitions
- Cell-line–derived organoids are 3D structures generated from established cell lines (tumor or normal) that grow in extracellular matrix gels under culture conditions providing key niche signals; they aim to recapitulate aspects of tissue architecture and function in vitro. <cite id="41cdde67-0">Compared to patient-derived organoids (PDOs), reviews explicitly contrast 2D/3D culture cell lines with PDOs for drug screening and model utility</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Use of organoids alongside cell-line experiments can strengthen findings, as shown in ER-stress studies in HCT116 cells and colonic PDOs treated with LPS</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Cell-derived organoids can be built from tumor cell lines, stem cells, or specialized cell lines in defined 3D scaffolds; the stability and long-term passaging history of cell lines can yield consistent organoid formation and mitigate sample availability limits</cite>.
- A key design principle is to supply endogenous niche signals (e.g., WNT/β-catenin, BMP inhibition, EGF/MAPK) to drive stemness, proliferation, and organogenesis. <cite id="e5feed20-0">Intestinal organoids pioneered this with R-spondin and WNT agonism plus Noggin/BMP inhibition and EGF in Matrigel to recreate crypt–villus architecture</cite>.

How cell line organoids are made: core protocols and factors
- Matrix and anchoring: <cite id="e5feed20-0">Cells are embedded in basement-membrane–mimetic hydrogels such as Matrigel that support self-assembly into crypt-like and villus-like domains when supplied with WNT, Noggin, R-spondin, and EGF</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Defined 3D scaffolds enable rebuilding of tissue structures and functions; engineered cell-line sources allow precise control over cellular composition and population dynamics</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Matrigel is an extract from mouse sarcoma and forms hydrogel at 30 °C+, widely effective for organoid generation but composition-variable and undefined</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-4">Ethical and standardization concerns around Matrigel motivate use of defined animal-free ECM alternatives for robust clinical translation</cite>.
- Canonical signaling cocktails for epithelial organoids:
  - WNT/β-catenin activation plus BMP inhibition: <cite id="e5feed20-0">R-spondin (WNT agonist) with Noggin (BMP inhibitor) and EGF supports long-term expansion of intestinal organoids with in vivo-like architecture</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-1">In endometrial epithelial gland organoids, titrating R-spondin (250–500 ng/mL) in Matrigel controlled growth; organoids expanded 1:2–1:4 and became predominantly epithelial after passages</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Colon cancer organoids grown in GFR Matrigel used conditioned media or defined Wnt3a/R-spondin3 with Noggin; PORCN inhibitor (Wnt-C59) or GSK inhibitor (IWP2) blocked WNT ligand signaling, enabling dependency readouts</cite>.
  - Fibroblast or conditioned-media support: <cite id="e5feed20-3">Intestinal subepithelial fibroblasts produce Wnt and R-spondin and can support organoid growth without exogenous ligands; however, APC deficiency or β-catenin mutations enable WNT/R-spondin–independent growth, and GSK3β inhibitors can substitute in mouse but are generally toxic to human intestinal organoids</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Immortalized myofibroblasts provide conditioned media to supply Wnt and other factors</cite>.
  - Alternative niche factors per organ: <cite id="e5feed20-0">Intestinal protocols established a template later adapted to colon and stomach cells with Lgr5+ stemness</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-3">Gastric/foregut organoids require FGF, retinoic acid, BMP inhibition (Noggin), and EGF/RA programs to drive endocrine lineage; ROCK/GSK inhibitors and Wnt3a are critical in gastric cancer organoids</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-4">A detailed colorectal organoid medium includes Wnt3a or human AFM/Wnt-3a conditioned media, R-spondin1-conditioned medium, Noggin, EGF, B27, N-acetylcysteine, nicotinamide, SB202190, A83-01, PGE2, gastrin, and antibiotics</cite>.
- Passaging and maintenance: <cite id="e5feed20-1">Endometrial organoids in Matrigel fragment and reassemble; 8–10 days of culture yields ~1:2–1:4 expansion, with predominance of epithelial cells after 1–2 passages and continued cystic growth beyond 20 passages</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Cell-line organoids can be directly edited (CRISPR) and tuned at the cellular level, with primary tumor-derived organoids from engineered lines forming within days in collagen scaffolds (e.g., osteosarcoma; chondrocyte/SW1353 cartilage in collagen)</cite>.

Tissue-specific examples using established cell lines
- Intestine/colon: <cite id="e5feed20-0">The R-spondin/WNT/Noggin/EGF Matrigel system first demonstrated robust intestinal organoids that recapitulate crypt–villus organization</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Colon cancer organoids using L-WRN conditioned media (Wnt3a, R-spondin, Noggin) expand and enable functional WNT/R-spondin dependency assays with pharmacologic inhibitors</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">HCT116 cells and colonic PDOs both show ER-stress responses modulated by naltrexone, supporting cross-validation of drug mechanisms alongside cell-line and organoid models</cite>.
- Bone/cartilage: <cite id="41cdde67-4">Osteosarcoma lines and chondrosarcoma lines (e.g., SW1353) form organoids in collagen-based matrices; engineered osteosarcoma lines with RB1/TP53 deletions generated organoids within 6 days in ECM, enabling direct comparison to primary tumor organoids</cite>.
- Endometrium: <cite id="e5feed20-1">Endometrial epithelial gland organoids in Matrigel respond to R-spondin dose with controlled growth and efficient passaging; medium optimization addresses space-limitation effects in gels</cite>.
- Liver: <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">HepG2, Hep3B, Huh-7 and other hepatocellular carcinoma lines can form organoid-like structures in Matrigel by day 9, with hepatocyte-like morphology and lineage marker expression; spheroids are irregular for mesenchymal-like lines</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Primary hepatocyte liver organoids in ECM show 3D spheroid formation with co-culture of mesenchymal cells; Matrigel-based systems demonstrate effectiveness but often lack full function/maturation and face composition uncertainty</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-4">Calls for transplantable liver organoids emphasize the need for defined, animal-free ECM matrices and guidelines for heterogeneity and functionality across organoid cell types</cite>.
- Foregut/neural precursors: <cite id="e5feed20-3">PSC-derived foregut organoids use activin A to definitive endoderm, FGF4 to anterior/foregut, GSK3β and BMP inhibition (CHIR99021, Noggin), and retinoic acid to drive endocrine (e.g., G cells); similar signaling logic applies when adapting tumor cell-line organoids with endocrine or neuroendocrine features</cite>.
- Cross-tissue generality of Matrigel 3D culture: <cite id="7d57e7ea-0">Matrigel-based organoid generation parallels intestine, kidney, and brain systems, enabling self-organization from iPSC/primary progenitors; the same platform has been adapted to many tissues</cite>.

Relationship to patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and to 2D lines
- Cross-validation and scalability: <cite id="41cdde67-2">Running organoids alongside 2D cell lines can strengthen mechanistic conclusions; for example, both HCT116 cells and patient-derived colonic organoids showed reduced ER stress with naltrexone</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">PDO libraries (e.g., 66 pancreatic organoids) correlate chemotherapy sensitivity with patient response, highlighting translational value</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-0">Reviews compare 2D/3D cell-line cultures with PDOs for drug screening, emphasizing that 3D culture improves functional readouts relative to 2D monolayers</cite>.
- Advantages of cell-line organoids: <cite id="41cdde67-4">Because cell lines are stable, passaged populations, organoids derived from them can be more consistent and easier to engineer (gene editing, defined genotypes), and they avoid donor and ethical constraints</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">For primary bone tumor organoids, cell-derived organoids can be directly adjusted at the cellular level compared to tissue-derived organoids, and can form rapidly in ECM</cite>.
- Caveats and limitations: <cite id="e5feed20-0">Immortalized human lines like HeLa have genomic instability and limited tissue identity, which has driven recent emphasis on stem-cell–derived organoids for genomic integrity and long-term expansion</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Matrigel’s undefined composition and mouse origin limit standardization and regulatory readiness; non-Matrigel ECMs are being sought to improve reproducibility</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Liver organoid function and maturation are often incomplete in Matrigel-based systems, reflecting challenges in replicating in vivo maturation cues</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">For certain primary tumors (e.g., chondrosarcoma, clear cell sarcoma), no established cell-line organoid protocols exist yet, and metastatic dynamics may introduce genetic/phenotypic heterogeneity that must be interpreted carefully</cite>.

Applications and use cases
- Drug screening and mechanism-of-action validation: <cite id="41cdde67-2">Organoids from pancreatic cancer PDOs aligned with patient outcomes in chemotherapy sensitivity, enabling pipelines tailored to organoid systems</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Side-by-side experiments with HCT116 cells and colonic organoids confirmed pharmacologic modulation of ER-stress pathways by naltrexone, illustrating orthogonal validation</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Wnt/R-spondin dependency assays in CRC organoids with pharmacologic inhibitors (Wnt-C59, IWP2) demonstrate functional pathway testing platforms</cite>.
- Disease modeling and lineage biology: <cite id="e5feed20-0">Adult stem-cell organoid systems have illuminated tissue maintenance and repair, and the same niche-factor logic (WNT, BMP inhibition, EGF) is leveraged to steer differentiation and growth</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-3">Foregut organoids show how FGF/RA/CHIR/Noggin programs generate lineage-specific endocrine organoids, informing cancer and development studies</cite>.
- Engineering and phenotypic interrogation: <cite id="41cdde67-4">Cell-line organoids are amenable to CRISPR and direct cellular editing; engineered osteosarcoma lines with RB1/TP53 loss formed organoids in collagen within days, enabling rapid phenotyping</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">Hepatoblast-like HCC lines (HepG2, Hep3B, Huh7) produced organoid-like structures with hepatocyte lineage markers, providing alternatives to 2D cultures for line-specific phenotypes</cite>.

Practical guidance and pitfalls
- Choosing a system: 
  - Epithelial organoids with Lgr5+ stemness (gut, stomach): prioritize WNT/R-spondin, Noggin, EGF; consider fibroblast co-culture or conditioned media. <cite id="e5feed20-0">The R-spondin/WNT/Noggin/EGF Matrigel method reliably expands intestinal organoids with in vivo-like architecture</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-3">FGF/RA/CHIR/Noggin programs drive endocrine lineage; ROCK/GSK inhibitors and Wnt3a are critical for gastric cancer organoids</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Conditioned media from WNT-active or R-spondin-producing fibroblasts can substitute for exogenous ligand supply</cite>.
  - Endometrium: start with R-spondin titration to balance growth and space constraints in Matrigel. <cite id="e5feed20-1">250–500 ng/mL R-spondin1 supports formation; 250 ng/mL often yields better growth due to gel space limits</cite>.
  - Liver/HCC: Matrigel-based 3D culture of hepatocyte lines to day 9; assess hepatocyte vs progenitor markers and heterogeneity. <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">HepG2/Huh7/Hep3B lines form organoid-like structures with hepatocyte lineage markers; mesenchymal-like lines form looser colonies</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Consider ECM choice carefully; Matrigel supports growth but may limit maturation</cite>.
  - Bone/cartilage: collagen matrices for chondrocyte/SW1353 and ECM for osteosarcoma; expect rapid formation after engineered-line introduction. <cite id="41cdde67-4">SW1353 cartilage forms organoids in collagen; osteosarcoma organoids formed within 6 days from engineered lines in ECM</cite>.
- Media and supplements: <cite id="e5feed20-4">A robust colorectal organoid medium combines Wnt3a or human AFM/Wnt-3a conditioned media, R-spondin1-conditioned medium, recombinant or conditioned Noggin, EGF, and antioxidants/metabolites (B27, NAC, nicotinamide), with SB202190, A83-01, PGE2, gastrin, and antibiotics</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-1">R-spondin dose and gel geometry impact growth kinetics; optimize split ratio to avoid overcrowding in wells</cite>.
- Quality control and drift: <cite id="e5feed20-0">HeLa-like lines can compromise genomic integrity and tissue identity; stem-derived organoids often provide better fidelity for healthy biology</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Despite stability from long-term culture, cell-line organoids still benefit from genotype tracking and periodic editing to probe oncogenic alterations; primary tumor organoids can be compared head-to-head with line-derived counterparts</cite>.
- Readouts and assays: <cite id="e5feed20-2">Biomarker panels and luciferase viability assays quantify growth; pharmacologic inhibitors (Wnt-C59, IWP2) test WNT dependency; conditioned media from WNT-active fibroblasts can rescue growth</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">Immunohistochemistry for hepatocyte lineage markers (e.g., hepatobiliary progenitor/hepatocyte markers) distinguishes organoid-like phenotypes from monolayer cultures</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Cross-model validation with matched cell lines and PDOs strengthens translational claims</cite>.

When cell-line organoids are most useful
- Rapid prototyping and hypothesis testing where a line’s genotype is known and manipulable, with need for scalable, low-variability models. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Stable long-term cell-line populations yield consistent organoid formation and allow precise control and engineering</cite>.
- Orthogonal validation pipelines for mechanism and efficacy. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Side-by-side HCT116 and colonic organoid results confirmed naltrexone’s ER-stress modulation; PDO drug-testing pipelines correlated with clinical response</cite>.
- Tissue systems with feasible protocols and defined signals. <cite id="e5feed20-0">Intestinal and gastric organoids have mature, well-characterized protocols leveraging WNT/BMP/EGF axes</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">HCC lines provide organoid-like structures amenable to hepatocyte-lineage analysis</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Bone/cartilage lines can form ECM-embedded organoids rapidly</cite>.

When to prefer primary-tissue or iPSC organoids
- Modeling healthy tissue homeostasis, development, or diseases with strong genomic fidelity requirements. <cite id="e5feed20-0">Stem-cell organoids enhance genomic integrity and long-term expansion while modeling healthy biology with robust niche-factor control</cite>.
- Avoiding genetic drift in non-transformed tissues or when patient-specificity matters. <cite id="41cdde67-0">PDO-focused reviews emphasize patient-matched organoids for drug screening and clinical decision making</cite>.
- Standardization and regulatory readiness where undefined matrices are a bottleneck. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Matrigel’s undefined composition and mouse origin impede standardization; defined animal-free ECMs are actively sought</cite>.

Key takeaways and decision checklist
- What you can do with cell-line organoids: rapid 3D models from known genotypes; orthogonal validation vs 2D lines; pharmacologic pathway testing; lineage marker profiling; scalable drug screening surrogates. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Running organoids alongside cell lines strengthens conclusions</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Pathway dependency assays and inhibitor screens are feasible</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">Line-specific organoid phenotypes are observable by lineage markers</cite>.
- What to watch: genomic instability in some lines; gel-induced variability (Matrigel composition); incomplete maturation in some organ systems; need for genotype tracking and editing; careful interpretation of metastatic-line models. <cite id="e5feed20-0">HeLa-like lines have genomic instability and limited tissue identity</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Matrigel variability limits standardization and maturation</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Some primary tumor organoids (e.g., chondrosarcoma, clear cell sarcoma) lack established cell-line protocols and remain challenging</cite>.
- If you choose a platform, start with a validated niche-factor recipe for your tissue, define your ECM and supplements, set R-spondin/WNT and BMP-inhibitor baselines, add EGF when needed, and benchmark against matched 2D cells and, where possible, PDOs. <cite id="e5feed20-0">Canonical intestinal niche factors drive organoid expansion and architecture</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-1">R-spondin titration and gel geometry impact growth kinetics</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-4">Detailed media recipes (Wnt3a/Rspo/Noggin/EGF plus metabolites and kinase inhibitors) show feasibility</cite>.

Open questions and active areas
- Defined ECMs for clinical translation: <cite id="7d57e7ea-4">Transplantable liver organoids argue for defined, animal-free matrices and standardized functional guidelines to move beyond Matrigel</cite>.
- Line selection and drift control: <cite id="e5feed20-0">Because genomic integrity and tissue identity can erode in some immortalized lines, careful line selection and periodic editing are prudent</cite>.
- Cross-organ protocols: while intestinal/gastric and hepatic systems are mature, standardized, high-fidelity protocols for neural and muscle organoids from non-stem lines remain less established and often require co-factor discovery and donor tissue integration. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Neuroectoderm and mesoderm organoid categories are cataloged, but practical cell-line protocols lag behind epithelial systems</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">No established cell-line organoid systems exist for some primary bone tumors, underscoring organ- and line-specific development needs</cite>.

Title: A novel perspective on bone tumors: advances in organoid research
Snippet: Cell-derived organoids are developed from a single cell type or line. Commonly used cell sources include tumor cell lines, stem cells, or specific osteoblasts (such as osteoblast cell lines or bone marrow stromal cells). Under specific culture media, these cells depend on 3D scaffolds to rebuilding structures and functions similar to those of the original tissue. The controllable nature of cell-derived organoids enables researchers to precisely regulate cellular composition and population dynamics. Furthermore, cell lines represent stable populations that have undergone long-term culture and passaging, resulting in greater consistency in organoid formation and experimental outcomes, while mitigating limitations associated with sample availability. 

In studies involving primary bone tumor organoids, cell-derived organoids can be directly adjusted at the cellular level using modern gene editing technologies, compared to tissue-derived organoids. For example, primary OS derived from animal models with double knockouts of RB1 and TP53, or triple knockouts of p53, Rb1, and SK2, was dissociated into single-cell suspensions and expanded into organoid cultures. OS organoids formed within 6 days (Wang et al., 2024). In establishing CS organoids, the SW1353 CS cell line is often used for culture, since the cartilage lacks blood vessels and has a greater matrix composition. In a study, Veys cultured the SW1353 and human articular chondrocytes within collagen scaffolds and analyzed cell cycle progression after 72 h (Veys et al., 2021). Despite these advancements in the development of organoids for primary bone tumor, no research has shown cellderived organoid establishment for CMA, ES, or MGCTB. 

In metastatic bone tumors studies, the cell source is typically derived from the metastatic cell lines from the primary sites. During metastasis, tumor cells undergo various biological changes, including enhanced invasiveness, migration ability, and adaptability to various microenvironments, along with genetic and phenotypic alterations. Therefore, using cell lines from the primary site closely represents the early dynamics of tumor metastasis, exhibiting stronger metastatic potential. In BCa BoM, the MDA-MB-231 cell line is highly metastatic.

Title: The Use of Stem Cell-Derived Organoids in Disease Modeling: An Update
Snippet: Human ASC-based organoids have been used to model several diseases, including cancer, infectious diseases, and inheritable genetic disorders. There have been many studies over the past decades, which have investigated signaling pathways through modeling human disease biology. This has provided an extensive understanding of adult tissue maintenance and repair [227]. 

Due to the genomic instability and limited amount of tissue identities within HeLa cells and other immortalized human cell lines [228], the focus of recent studies switched to in vitro models derived from stem cells. This has permitted a wider array of tissue identities to be identified, enhanced genomic integrity, long-term expansion, and improved modeling of healthy biology. Traditionally, studies using human disease tissues had constraints related to availability of the native disease tissue, restricted accessibility to the tissue, and ethical concerns. The fact that organoids can be established from a small amount of tissue and can be rapidly and effortlessly cultured makes them adequate models for studying multiple diseases [229]. 

In 2009, the stem cells field has witnessed a major methodical advance by the successful development of the intestinal organoid culture system referred to as the R-spondin method [230]. The tumor microenvironment contains tumor cells and stromal cells supporting cancer development. These ASC-derived organoids are embedded in a matrix simple, called Matrigel supplemented with different growth factors establishing key endogenous niche signals: WNT, a Frizzled/LRP (lipoprotein receptor-related protein) ligand; Noggin (an inhibitor of bone morphogenetic protein) for stem cell expansion; R-spondin (a WNT agonist) for maintaining stem cell populations; and EGF for promoting cell proliferation. This system was used to create 3D structures with distinct crypt-like and villus-like domains [3]. Remarkably, these organoids dependably recapitulated the in vivo tissue architecture. The system was subsequently adapted for not only generating human intestinal organoids, but also organoids derived from other organs, particularly from colon and stomach having Lgr5+ stem cells [230][231][232][233].
</snippet>

Title: Investigating bacteria-induced inflammatory responses using novel endometrial epithelial gland organoid models
Snippet: Human endometrial epithelial glands were isolated and cultured in a three-dimensional Matrigel with conditioned medium (Figure 1A). Immunofluorescence staining revealed strong expression of MUC1, E-Cadherin, and EpCAM in epithelial cells and gland fragments isolated from endometrial biopsies (Figure 1B). In a specific culture system utilizing Matrigel and conditions, EEGOs were generated from endometrial tissues and readily formed within a week, growing into large spherical structures (Figure 1C). Given that R-Spondin-1 amplifies the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, maintaining stemness while promoting the self-renewal of stem cells, R-Spondin-1 concentrations of 500 ng/ml and 250 ng/ml were selected for culturing the organoids. While the higher concentration allows for more organoids, the limited space in the Matrigel impedes further expansion of the organoids. Therefore, the organoids cultured with 250 ng/ml R-Spondin-1 grew better (Figure 1D). Organoid counts and diameter measurements were conducted on days 3, 5, and 7 respectively (Figures 1E,F). Organoids on day 5 exhibited statistically significant differences in number and growth diameter compared to day 3 (p < 0.05). After 8-10 days of culture, the organoids expanded at a 1:2 or 1:4 ratio, then dissociated into cell clusters that regenerated into new organoids. After 1-2 passages, no stromal cells were observed, and the organoids have now exceeded 20 passages, maintaining a rounded cystic structure (Figure 1G).

Title: Human iPS derived progenitors bioengineered into liver organoids using an inverted colloidal crystal poly (ethylene glycol) scaffold
Snippet: Induced pluripotent stem cells offer exciting new possibilities in developmental biology, disease modelling and transplantation. Comprehensive realization of that promise is likely to require consolidation with other emerging technologies such as 3D cell culture. Along those lines, hepatic progenitor cells derived from iPSCs [1] and primary tissue [2] were recently shown to form "Organoids" (self-organising miniaturized 3D structures resembling liver tissue) following 3D culture initiated by Matrigel. Organoid generation using Matrigel has similarly been demonstrated across a broad range of tissue types including intestine, kidney and brain [3e5], underlining the importance of this novel approach across the stem cell field. Downstream applications are however limited by the use of Matrigel which is poorly characterized, highly variable and of mouse origin [6]. A bioengineered substitute is therefore essential and was recently reported for intestinal organoid generation [7]. A similar bottom up engineering approach for liver organoid production is urgently needed. We recently developed a novel hepatocyte culture system composed of a 3D-hexagonally arrayed inverted colloidal crystal (ICC) scaffold [8]. In comparison to other 3D culture systems, the ICC boasts several advantages. These include being made from an FDA approved material, polyethylene glycol (PEG), that can be functionalized with select ECM proteins or varied in mechanical stiffness, a highly uniform architecture which incorporates sizeselectable pores to facilitate tissue interconnection across the whole module whilst retaining uniform nutrient penetration to all cells and finally, being transparent to provide an easy means of viewing cells and intra-cellular fluorescence over time. Exploiting these properties, we were able to facilitate induction of organoid structures with advanced liver function in primary human fetal liver cells cultured in ICC's [9]. Lack of donor material, ethical constraints and biological heterogeneity however make further progress difficult with human fetal cells. We therefore turned to the recently established technology of human iPSC-derived hepatocytes [10,11], as a good biological approximation to human fetal liver cells but not limited by the same constraints cited above, to explore their potential for organoid generation.
</snippet>

Below is a concise, evidence-backed overview of “cell line organoids” (organoids derived from established 2D cell lines), how they are built, what they can do, and how they compare with organoids derived from fresh tissues or iPSCs.

Overview and definitions
- Cell-line–derived organoids are 3D structures generated from established cell lines (tumor or normal) that grow in extracellular matrix gels under culture conditions providing key niche signals; they aim to recapitulate aspects of tissue architecture and function in vitro. <cite id="41cdde67-0">Compared to patient-derived organoids (PDOs), reviews explicitly contrast 2D/3D culture cell lines with PDOs for drug screening and model utility</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Use of organoids alongside cell-line experiments can strengthen findings, as shown in ER-stress studies in HCT116 cells and colonic PDOs treated with LPS</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Cell-derived organoids can be built from tumor cell lines, stem cells, or specialized cell lines in defined 3D scaffolds; the stability and long-term passaging history of cell lines can yield consistent organoid formation and mitigate sample availability limits</cite>.
- A key design principle is to supply endogenous niche signals (e.g., WNT/β-catenin, BMP inhibition, EGF/MAPK) to drive stemness, proliferation, and organogenesis. <cite id="e5feed20-0">Intestinal organoids pioneered this with R-spondin and WNT agonism plus Noggin/BMP inhibition and EGF in Matrigel to recreate crypt–villus architecture</cite>.

How cell line organoids are made: core protocols and factors
- Matrix and anchoring: <cite id="e5feed20-0">Cells are embedded in basement-membrane–mimetic hydrogels such as Matrigel that support self-assembly into crypt-like and villus-like domains when supplied with WNT, Noggin, R-spondin, and EGF</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Defined 3D scaffolds enable rebuilding of tissue structures and functions; engineered cell-line sources allow precise control over cellular composition and population dynamics</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Matrigel is an extract from mouse sarcoma and forms hydrogel at 30 °C+, widely effective for organoid generation but composition-variable and undefined</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-4">Ethical and standardization concerns around Matrigel motivate use of defined animal-free ECM alternatives for robust clinical translation</cite>.
- Canonical signaling cocktails for epithelial organoids:
  - WNT/β-catenin activation plus BMP inhibition: <cite id="e5feed20-0">R-spondin (WNT agonist) with Noggin (BMP inhibitor) and EGF supports long-term expansion of intestinal organoids with in vivo-like architecture</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-1">In endometrial epithelial gland organoids, titrating R-spondin (250–500 ng/mL) in Matrigel controlled growth; organoids expanded 1:2–1:4 and became predominantly epithelial after passages</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Colon cancer organoids grown in GFR Matrigel used conditioned media or defined Wnt3a/R-spondin3 with Noggin; PORCN inhibitor (Wnt-C59) or GSK inhibitor (IWP2) blocked WNT ligand signaling, enabling dependency readouts</cite>.
  - Fibroblast or conditioned-media support: <cite id="e5feed20-3">Intestinal subepithelial fibroblasts produce Wnt and R-spondin and can support organoid growth without exogenous ligands; however, APC deficiency or β-catenin mutations enable WNT/R-spondin–independent growth, and GSK3β inhibitors can substitute in mouse but are generally toxic to human intestinal organoids</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Immortalized myofibroblasts provide conditioned media to supply Wnt and other factors</cite>.
  - Alternative niche factors per organ: <cite id="e5feed20-0">Intestinal protocols established a template later adapted to colon and stomach cells with Lgr5+ stemness</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-3">Gastric/foregut organoids require FGF, retinoic acid, BMP inhibition (Noggin), and EGF/RA programs to drive endocrine lineage; ROCK/GSK inhibitors and Wnt3a are critical in gastric cancer organoids</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-4">A detailed colorectal organoid medium includes Wnt3a or human AFM/Wnt-3a conditioned media, R-spondin1-conditioned medium, Noggin, EGF, B27, N-acetylcysteine, nicotinamide, SB202190, A83-01, PGE2, gastrin, and antibiotics</cite>.
- Passaging and maintenance: <cite id="e5feed20-1">Endometrial organoids in Matrigel fragment and reassemble; 8–10 days of culture yields ~1:2–1:4 expansion, with predominance of epithelial cells after 1–2 passages and continued cystic growth beyond 20 passages</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Cell-line organoids can be directly edited (CRISPR) and tuned at the cellular level, with primary tumor-derived organoids from engineered lines forming within days in collagen scaffolds (e.g., osteosarcoma; chondrocyte/SW1353 cartilage in collagen)</cite>.

Tissue-specific examples using established cell lines
- Intestine/colon: <cite id="e5feed20-0">The R-spondin/WNT/Noggin/EGF Matrigel system first demonstrated robust intestinal organoids that recapitulate crypt–villus organization</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Colon cancer organoids using L-WRN conditioned media (Wnt3a, R-spondin, Noggin) expand and enable functional WNT/R-spondin dependency assays with pharmacologic inhibitors</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">HCT116 cells and colonic PDOs both show ER-stress responses modulated by naltrexone, supporting cross-validation of drug mechanisms alongside cell-line and organoid models</cite>.
- Bone/cartilage: <cite id="41cdde67-4">Osteosarcoma lines and chondrosarcoma lines (e.g., SW1353) form organoids in collagen-based matrices; engineered osteosarcoma lines with RB1/TP53 deletions generated organoids within 6 days in ECM, enabling direct comparison to primary tumor organoids</cite>.
- Endometrium: <cite id="e5feed20-1">Endometrial epithelial gland organoids in Matrigel respond to R-spondin dose with controlled growth and efficient passaging; medium optimization addresses space-limitation effects in gels</cite>.
- Liver: <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">HepG2, Hep3B, Huh-7 and other hepatocellular carcinoma lines can form organoid-like structures in Matrigel by day 9, with hepatocyte-like morphology and lineage marker expression; spheroids are irregular for mesenchymal-like lines</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Primary hepatocyte liver organoids in ECM show 3D spheroid formation with co-culture of mesenchymal cells; Matrigel-based systems demonstrate effectiveness but often lack full function/maturation and face composition uncertainty</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-4">Calls for transplantable liver organoids emphasize the need for defined, animal-free ECM matrices and guidelines for heterogeneity and functionality across organoid cell types</cite>.
- Foregut/neural precursors: <cite id="e5feed20-3">PSC-derived foregut organoids use activin A to definitive endoderm, FGF4 to anterior/foregut, GSK3β and BMP inhibition (CHIR99021, Noggin), and retinoic acid to drive endocrine (e.g., G cells); similar signaling logic applies when adapting tumor cell-line organoids with endocrine or neuroendocrine features</cite>.
- Cross-tissue generality of Matrigel 3D culture: <cite id="7d57e7ea-0">Matrigel-based organoid generation parallels intestine, kidney, and brain systems, enabling self-organization from iPSC/primary progenitors; the same platform has been adapted to many tissues</cite>.

Relationship to patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and to 2D lines
- Cross-validation and scalability: <cite id="41cdde67-2">Running organoids alongside 2D cell lines can strengthen mechanistic conclusions; for example, both HCT116 cells and patient-derived colonic organoids showed reduced ER stress with naltrexone</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">PDO libraries (e.g., 66 pancreatic organoids) correlate chemotherapy sensitivity with patient response, highlighting translational value</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-0">Reviews compare 2D/3D cell-line cultures with PDOs for drug screening, emphasizing that 3D culture improves functional readouts relative to 2D monolayers</cite>.
- Advantages of cell-line organoids: <cite id="41cdde67-4">Because cell lines are stable, passaged populations, organoids derived from them can be more consistent and easier to engineer (gene editing, defined genotypes), and they avoid donor and ethical constraints</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">For primary bone tumor organoids, cell-derived organoids can be directly adjusted at the cellular level compared to tissue-derived organoids, and can form rapidly in ECM</cite>.
- Caveats and limitations: <cite id="e5feed20-0">Immortalized human lines like HeLa have genomic instability and limited tissue identity, which has driven recent emphasis on stem-cell–derived organoids for genomic integrity and long-term expansion</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Matrigel’s undefined composition and mouse origin limit standardization and regulatory readiness; non-Matrigel ECMs are being sought to improve reproducibility</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Liver organoid function and maturation are often incomplete in Matrigel-based systems, reflecting challenges in replicating in vivo maturation cues</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">For certain primary tumors (e.g., chondrosarcoma, clear cell sarcoma), no established cell-line organoid protocols exist yet, and metastatic dynamics may introduce genetic/phenotypic heterogeneity that must be interpreted carefully</cite>.

Applications and use cases
- Drug screening and mechanism-of-action validation: <cite id="41cdde67-2">Organoids from pancreatic cancer PDOs aligned with patient outcomes in chemotherapy sensitivity, enabling pipelines tailored to organoid systems</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Side-by-side experiments with HCT116 cells and colonic organoids confirmed pharmacologic modulation of ER-stress pathways by naltrexone, illustrating orthogonal validation</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Wnt/R-spondin dependency assays in CRC organoids with pharmacologic inhibitors (Wnt-C59, IWP2) demonstrate functional pathway testing platforms</cite>.
- Disease modeling and lineage biology: <cite id="e5feed20-0">Adult stem-cell organoid systems have illuminated tissue maintenance and repair, and the same niche-factor logic (WNT, BMP inhibition, EGF) is leveraged to steer differentiation and growth</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-3">Foregut organoids show how FGF/RA/CHIR/Noggin programs generate lineage-specific endocrine organoids, informing cancer and development studies</cite>.
- Engineering and phenotypic interrogation: <cite id="41cdde67-4">Cell-line organoids are amenable to CRISPR and direct cellular editing; engineered osteosarcoma lines with RB1/TP53 loss formed organoids in collagen within days, enabling rapid phenotyping</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">Hepatoblast-like HCC lines (HepG2, Hep3B, Huh7) produced organoid-like structures with hepatocyte lineage markers, providing alternatives to 2D cultures for line-specific phenotypes</cite>.

Practical guidance and pitfalls
- Choosing a system: 
  - Epithelial organoids with Lgr5+ stemness (gut, stomach): prioritize WNT/R-spondin, Noggin, EGF; consider fibroblast co-culture or conditioned media. <cite id="e5feed20-0">The R-spondin/WNT/Noggin/EGF Matrigel method reliably expands intestinal organoids with in vivo-like architecture</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-3">FGF/RA/CHIR/Noggin programs drive endocrine lineage; ROCK/GSK inhibitors and Wnt3a are critical for gastric cancer organoids</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-2">Conditioned media from WNT-active or R-spondin-producing fibroblasts can substitute for exogenous ligand supply</cite>.
  - Endometrium: start with R-spondin titration to balance growth and space constraints in Matrigel. <cite id="e5feed20-1">250–500 ng/mL R-spondin1 supports formation; 250 ng/mL often yields better growth due to gel space limits</cite>.
  - Liver/HCC: Matrigel-based 3D culture of hepatocyte lines to day 9; assess hepatocyte vs progenitor markers and heterogeneity. <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">HepG2/Huh7/Hep3B lines form organoid-like structures with hepatocyte lineage markers; mesenchymal-like lines form looser colonies</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-3">Consider ECM choice carefully; Matrigel supports growth but may limit maturation</cite>.
  - Bone/cartilage: collagen matrices for chondrocyte/SW1353 and ECM for osteosarcoma; expect rapid formation after engineered-line introduction. <cite id="41cdde67-4">SW1353 cartilage forms organoids in collagen; osteosarcoma organoids formed within 6 days from engineered lines in ECM</cite>.
- Media and supplements: <cite id="e5feed20-4">A robust colorectal organoid medium combines Wnt3a or human AFM/Wnt-3a conditioned media, R-spondin1-conditioned medium, recombinant or conditioned Noggin, EGF, and antioxidants/metabolites (B27, NAC, nicotinamide), with SB202190, A83-01, PGE2, gastrin, and antibiotics</cite>. <cite id="e5feed20-1">R-spondin dose and gel geometry impact growth kinetics; optimize split ratio to avoid overcrowding in wells</cite>.
- Quality control and drift: <cite id="e5feed20-0">HeLa-like lines can compromise genomic integrity and tissue identity; stem-derived organoids often provide better fidelity for healthy biology</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Despite stability from long-term culture, cell-line organoids still benefit from genotype tracking and periodic editing to probe oncogenic alterations; primary tumor organoids can be compared head-to-head with line-derived counterparts</cite>.
- Readouts and assays: <cite id="e5feed20-2">Biomarker panels and luciferase viability assays quantify growth; pharmacologic inhibitors (Wnt-C59, IWP2) test WNT dependency; conditioned media from WNT-active fibroblasts can rescue growth</cite>. <cite id="7d57e7ea-2">Immunohistochemistry for hepatocyte lineage markers (e.g., hepatobiliary progenitor/hepatocyte markers) distinguishes organoid-like phenotypes from monolayer cultures</cite>. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Cross-model validation with matched cell lines and PDOs strengthens translational claims</cite>.

When cell-line organoids are most useful
- Rapid prototyping and hypothesis testing where a line’s genotype is known and manipulable, with need for scalable, low-variability models. <cite id="41cdde67-4">Stable long-term cell-line populations yield consistent organoid formation and allow precise control and engineering</cite>.
- Orthogonal validation pipelines for mechanism and efficacy. <cite id="41cdde67-2">Side-by-side HCT116 and colonic organoid results confirmed naltrexone’s ER-stress modulation; PDO drug-testing pipelines correlated with clinical response</cite>.

Title: A novel perspective on bone tumors: advances in organoid research
Snippet: Cell-derived organoids are developed from a single cell type or line. Commonly used cell sources include tumor cell lines, stem cells, or specific osteoblasts (such as osteoblast cell lines or bone marrow stromal cells). Under specific culture media, these cells depend on 3D scaffolds to rebuilding structures and functions similar to those of the original tissue. The controllable nature of cell-derived organoids enables researchers to precisely regulate cellular composition and population dynamics. Furthermore, cell lines represent stable populations that have undergone long-term culture and passaging, resulting in greater consistency in organoid formation and experimental outcomes, while mitigating limitations associated with sample availability. 

In studies involving primary bone tumor organoids, cell-derived organoids can be directly adjusted at the cellular level using modern gene editing technologies, compared to tissue-derived organoids. For example, primary OS derived from animal models with double knockouts of RB1 and TP53, or triple knockouts of p53, Rb1, and SK2, was dissociated into single-cell suspensions and expanded into organoid cultures. OS organoids formed within 6 days (Wang et al., 2024). In establishing CS organoids, the SW1353 CS cell line is often used for culture, since the cartilage lacks blood vessels and has a greater matrix composition. In a study, Veys cultured the SW1353 and human articular chondrocytes within collagen scaffolds and analyzed cell cycle progression after 72 h (Veys et al., 2021). Despite these advancements in the development of organoids for primary bone tumor, no research has shown cellderived organoid establishment for CMA, ES, or MGCTB. 

In metastatic bone tumors studies, the cell source is typically derived from the metastatic cell lines from the primary sites. During metastasis, tumor cells undergo various biological changes, including enhanced invasiveness, migration ability, and adaptability to various microenvironments, along with genetic and phenotypic alterations. Therefore, using cell lines from the primary site closely represents the early dynamics of tumor metastasis, exhibiting stronger metastatic potential. In BCa BoM, the MDA-MB-231 cell line is highly metastatic.

Title: The Use of Stem Cell-Derived Organoids in Disease Modeling: An Update
Snippet: Human ASC-based organoids have been used to model several diseases, including cancer, infectious diseases, and inheritable genetic disorders. There have been many studies over the past decades, which have investigated signaling pathways through modeling human disease biology. This has provided an extensive understanding of adult tissue maintenance and repair [227]. 

Due to the genomic instability and limited amount of tissue identities within HeLa cells and other immortalized human cell lines [228], the focus of recent studies switched to in vitro models derived from stem cells. This has permitted a wider array of tissue identities to be identified, enhanced genomic integrity, long-term expansion, and improved modeling of healthy biology. Traditionally, studies using human disease tissues had constraints related to availability of the native disease tissue, restricted accessibility to the tissue, and ethical concerns. The fact that organoids can be established from a small amount of tissue and can be rapidly and effortlessly cultured makes them adequate models for studying multiple diseases [229]. 

In 2009, the stem cells field has witnessed a major methodical advance by the successful development of the intestinal organoid culture system referred to as the R-spondin method [230]. The tumor microenvironment contains tumor cells and stromal cells supporting cancer development. These ASC-derived organoids are embedded in a matrix simple, called Matrigel supplemented with different growth factors establishing key endogenous niche signals: WNT, a Frizzled/LRP (lipoprotein receptor-related protein) ligand; Noggin (an inhibitor of bone morphogenetic protein) for stem cell expansion; R-spondin (a WNT agonist) for maintaining stem cell populations; and EGF for promoting cell proliferation. This system was used to create 3D structures with distinct crypt-like and villus-like domains [3]. Remarkably, these organoids dependably recapitulated the in vivo tissue architecture. The system was subsequently adapted for not only generating human intestinal organoids, but also organoids derived from other organs, particularly from colon and stomach having Lgr5+ stem cells [230][231][232][233].

Title: Investigating bacteria-induced inflammatory responses using novel endometrial epithelial gland organoid models
Snippet: Human endometrial epithelial glands were isolated and cultured in a three-dimensional Matrigel with conditioned medium (Figure 1A). Immunofluorescence staining revealed strong expression of MUC1, E-Cadherin, and EpCAM in epithelial cells and gland fragments isolated from endometrial biopsies (Figure 1B). In a specific culture system utilizing Matrigel and conditions, EEGOs were generated from endometrial tissues and readily formed within a week, growing into large spherical structures (Figure 1C). Given that R-Spondin-1 amplifies the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, maintaining stemness while promoting the self-renewal of stem cells, R-Spondin-1 concentrations of 500 ng/ml and 250 ng/ml were selected for culturing the organoids. While the higher concentration allows for more organoids, the limited space in the Matrigel impedes further expansion of the organoids. Therefore, the organoids cultured with 250 ng/ml R-Spondin-1 grew better (Figure 1D). Organoid counts and diameter measurements were conducted on days 3, 5, and 7 respectively (Figures 1E,F). Organoids on day 5 exhibited statistically significant differences in number and growth diameter compared to day 3 (p < 0.05). After 8-10 days of culture, the organoids expanded at a 1:2 or 1:4 ratio, then dissociated into cell clusters that regenerated into new organoids. After 1-2 passages, no stromal cells were observed, and the organoids have now exceeded 20 passages, maintaining a rounded cystic structure (Figure 1G).

Title: Human iPS derived progenitors bioengineered into liver organoids using an inverted colloidal crystal poly (ethylene glycol) scaffold
Snippet: Induced pluripotent stem cells offer exciting new possibilities in developmental biology, disease modelling and transplantation. Comprehensive realization of that promise is likely to require consolidation with other emerging technologies such as 3D cell culture. Along those lines, hepatic progenitor cells derived from iPSCs [1] and primary tissue [2] were recently shown to form "Organoids" (self-organising miniaturized 3D structures resembling liver tissue) following 3D culture initiated by Matrigel. Organoid generation using Matrigel has similarly been demonstrated across a broad range of tissue types including intestine, kidney and brain [3e5], underlining the importance of this novel approach across the stem cell field. Downstream applications are however limited by the use of Matrigel which is poorly characterized, highly variable and of mouse origin [6]. A bioengineered substitute is therefore essential and was recently reported for intestinal organoid generation [7]. A similar bottom up engineering approach for liver organoid production is urgently needed. We recently developed a novel hepatocyte culture system composed of a 3D-hexagonally arrayed inverted colloidal crystal (ICC) scaffold [8]. In comparison to other 3D culture systems, the ICC boasts several advantages. These include being made from an FDA approved material, polyethylene glycol (PEG), that can be functionalized with select ECM proteins or varied in mechanical stiffness, a highly uniform architecture which incorporates sizeselectable pores to facilitate tissue interconnection across the whole module whilst retaining uniform nutrient penetration to all cells and finally, being transparent to provide an easy means of viewing cells and intra-cellular fluorescence over time. Exploiting these properties, we were able to facilitate induction of organoid structures with advanced liver function in primary human fetal liver cells cultured in ICC's [9]. Lack of donor material, ethical constraints and biological heterogeneity however make further progress difficult with human fetal cells. We therefore turned to the recently established technology of human iPSC-derived hepatocytes [10,11], as a good biological approximation to human fetal liver cells but not limited by the same constraints cited above, to explore their potential for organoid generation.
